title: Remediate the open SonarCloud security and reliability findings on business scope
goal: Clear the SonarCloud quality-gate blockers for duanxldragon_pantheon-ops by fixing every open vulnerability and bug in the touched scope with real code, turning the 33-issue gosecurity:S3649 family into a machine-checked CI invariant, and only then transitioning the verified false positives in Sonar with a recorded, reversible justification.
dependsOn: 2026-10-29-sonar-ci-analysis-restore (the scan must run before its findings can be closed)
blocks: green SonarCloud quality gate on pantheon-ops main

in: ArgoCD client: always verify the server certificate; support private CAs through a stored PEM bundle instead of InsecureSkipVerify (go:S4830, go:S5527).
Filedist storage: confine resolved paths to the configured root and reduce upload names to one path element (gosecurity:S2083).
Add scripts/check-gorm-sql-literal.mjs plus node tests and a blocking docs-governance CI step so the S3649 false-positive argument is a checked invariant.
Fix the frontend floating-promise, nested-template, fixed-wait and cleartext-placeholder findings and the duplicated CI worker config in e2e-tests/playwright.config.ts.
Remove the hardcoded reachable target IP and implicit cleartext defaults from both e2e shell scripts by requiring explicit API_BASE_URL / WEB_BASE_URL.
Merge the byte-identical upgrade/rollback branches in service/state.go and move the CMDB import template example IP into the RFC 5737 documentation range.
Capture the S3649 issue keys, transition them with a written justification after the checker is merged, and read back the gate.

Clear the remaining 158 open CODE_SMELL findings on main so the hosted Issues counter reaches zero: go:S1192 x68, go:S3776 x27, typescript:S3358 x20, typescript:S3863 x10, godre:* x10, typescript:S3776 x6, typescript:S6571 x6, typescript:S6551 x3, go:S107 x2, go:S1135 x2, githubactions:S1192 x2, typescript:S7770 x1, typescript:S7755 x1, by real refactoring only (named constants, guard clauses, extracted helpers, named types, merged imports) with no suppression comment and no assertion weakened.
out: Any change to SonarCloud quality-gate definitions, the new-code period, or the organization plan.
Provisioning Dependabot secrets or changing the Dependabot scan policy.
Removing the external Vercel deployment check, which requires a maintainer action in the GitHub UI.
Adding a UI form for ArgoCD CA-certificate storage; caCert is API-only in this round.

Any rename that changes a JSON payload, a database column, a route path, an i18n key or a menu seed value; the smell refactor is behaviour-preserving by construction and is checked by the existing contract gates.
Clearing smells under frontend/src and pkg/ that belong to the base foundation rather than to business/*; the 158-issue inventory is entirely inside business scope plus two workflow files.

doNotTouch: sonar-project.properties and .sonarcloud.properties (project identity and analysis scope are settled)
any repository secret value inside the working tree; SONAR_TOKEN is only ever a shell variable

implementationNotes: SonarGo reports gosecurity:S3649 for any GORM condition argument that is not a source-level literal, including package-level constants that are provably literal. Arguing 33 findings by hand does not survive the next analysis, so the invariant behind the argument is now enforced by scripts/check-gorm-sql-literal.mjs, unit-tested by tests/scripts/check-gorm-sql-literal.test.mjs and blocking in the docs-governance job.

The checker distinguishes GORM sinks from same-named methods on other receivers (the Kubernetes clientset Update(ctx, object, opts) has a different arity) and treats line-scoped waivers as visible output, never as silence. An empty justification is not a waiver.

retired_modules.go previously passed a column name into a built clause; the three IN clauses became package constants, matching the condNameEquals and menuPathWhereClause convention already used by the CMDB modules, and the two remaining dynamic-looking call sites carry visible waivers.

ArgoCD server certificate verification is now unconditional. A stored CA bundle adds trust; an unparseable bundle fails construction with ErrInvalidCACert instead of silently downgrading. The tests inject the httptest server certificate as the stored bundle, so they exercise the production path rather than bypassing it.
biz_argocd_server.ca_cert needs no SQL migration: the argocd module owns Migrate() with GORM AutoMigrate and no versioned SQL references that table.

e2e-tests/auto-test.sh shipped a reachable production IP and http:// defaults; requiring API_BASE_URL and WEB_BASE_URL removes the shell:S5332 class instead of marking it won't-fix, and the same change makes the scripts refuse to run against an unintended host.
The checker is an Ops-only sensor: base ships no backend/modules/business, so it is deliberately not proposed upstream and must not be hand-copied into base.

Round 2 was driven by the first hosted CI run rather than by local review: Go Lint reported one new gosec G304 on the line this round introduced (os.Create of a path that is already proven to stay inside the storage root), annotated consistently with the three G304 waivers already in that module, and the SonarCloud gate stayed ERROR only on new-code duplication because the new checker test file repeated its twelve test bodies. The test file became a CASES table with one driver loop, so the duplication is removed rather than the metric suppressed; the gate's security and reliability conditions were already OK on that analysis.

Post-merge read-back (round 3): the squash-merge landed on main as 9522048 and the push-triggered scan took open issues from 242 to 194, bugs from 6 to 0, and new_reliability_rating to OK. The only remaining gate ERROR is new_security_rating, whose whole residue is 33 gosecurity:S3649 plus 3 gosecurity:S2083 on the os.Remove cleanup sites in UploadFile. SonarGo accepted resolveWithinRoot as a sanitizer for os.Create but not for os.Remove on the same value, so those three are backed by TestUploadPathStaysInsideRootForAdversarialNames, which pins the flagged data flow end to end, and by the checker for the S3649 family. Nothing was transitioned before that test was main-merged.

Round 4 executed the transition last, against the merged tree: the checker and its 13 tests were re-run green on 52dfe28, the packages hosting every still-open sink passed, and each of the 18 remaining S3649 lines was read to confirm it is an Updates(map) with quoted literal keys or a First(&model, id) primary-key lookup. All 36 keys are now RESOLVED/FALSE-POSITIVE, open vulnerabilities went 36 to 0, and the branch gate reads OK on every condition. POST /api/issues/comment is not exposed by SonarCloud (404 Unknown url), so the justification is carried by sonar-triage.json and this packet instead of the issue thread, and /api/issues/search ignores issueKeys while rejecting RESOLVED in issueStatuses, which is why live state is matched client-side. The transition driver stayed outside the repository because it authenticates with a maintainer token; reversibility is per key via transition=to_reopen and no metric, new-code baseline or gate definition was edited.

Round 5 targeted the maintainability residue instead of the gate: every one of the 158 open CODE_SMELL findings on main was mapped to a rule-specific fix and applied in the file that produced it. S1192 became package-level constants (never var, and never for the Updates(map) keys, because scripts/check-gorm-sql-literal.mjs requires those to stay quoted literals in place), S3776 became guard clauses and per-case helpers, S3358 became module-level if/else resolvers, S3863 became merged imports, S6571 became a named union with (string & {}), S6551 became typeof narrowing, S7755 became .at(-1), S8205 became named payload types, S8209 became grouped parameters, S8193 became inline expressions, and S8196 became agentive names for single-method interfaces (InstanceCreator, StateTransitioner, ServiceInstanceStateApplier, LogWriter).

The two go:S1135 TODO comments were resolved by their evidence, not by deleting the comment: the ArgoCD webhook auto-sync is now implemented behind an applicationSyncer seam with three tests (policy parsing, sync-only-automated, failure still marks the event processed), and the reconciler service-instance stub was deleted because biz_argocd_application carries no service-instance association, so faking it would have invented a data path the schema cannot express.

Two gate couplings were found the hard way and are now recorded rather than rediscovered. First, EXPECTED_RESULT in the aggregate steps is fail-closed: an unset env expands to an empty string, the comparison mismatches and the step exits 1, and the base-owned tests/scripts/security-workflow.test.mjs pins the literal "success" text in the dependency-vulnerabilities branch, so exactly one literal stays there and only the other four became ${EXPECTED_RESULT}. Second, frontend/scripts/check-menu-contract.mjs goConstTable() resolves a seed field identifier only from a `name = "value"` line inside a const block, so an inline const used by a menu seed silently resolves to an empty string; serviceModuleKey is therefore declared inside a const block and the generic checker improvement is a base-first follow-up.

Verification discipline for this round: a gocognit and duplicate-literal scan of HEAD versus the working tree is used as the resolution oracle, because SonarGo reports gocognit-equivalent complexity values that are never higher than gocognit, so a function that drops to 15 or fewer by gocognit cannot still be an S3776 finding; 27 of 27 Go S3776 targets are at or below the threshold and no new duplicate-literal candidate appeared anywhere in backend/modules/business.

Round 6 was driven by the PR-side analysis rather than by assumption: /api/issues/search?pullRequest=160 returns only new-code findings, and it reported 12 open issues on the lines this branch changes. Four were real regressions introduced by round 5 and are now fixed in place — go:S8242 (taskStepHostRun carried a context.Context as a struct field, so ctx is threaded through executeTaskStep and runTaskStepCheck instead), go:S3776 on buildDeployExecutionSnapshot (split into defaultExecutionSnapshotSteps, buildTemplateStepSnapshot, resolveStepSnapshotPackage and validateStepSnapshotParams with the two snapshot reason constants), go:S3776 on all three CMDB Import functions, and typescript:S6759 on the ClusterDetail hero and summary card props.

The CMDB Import refactor deliberately reuses the base-owned impexp primitives (BuildHeaderIndex, RequireHeaders, ForEachDataRow, AppendImportError) rather than adding three near-identical per-module header helpers, because a third copy of the same header-and-row loop would have raised new_duplicated_lines_density on the very analysis that is supposed to go green; only the per-module field parsing moved into parseGroupImportRows / parseLabelImportRows / parseHostImportRows.

Sonar tracks an issue instance by the text hash of its location, which is why round 4's FALSE_POSITIVE transitions are not free to rewrite: replacing a marked sink statement such as Where("id = ?", id) with a constant creates a new open instance at that statement. The four round-4-marked sinks in argocd_service.go and backup_service.go were therefore restored verbatim to their HEAD text, and the remaining occurrences in the same files moved to package constants; go:S1192 counts occurrences per file with a threshold of three, so each file keeps exactly two inline literals and stays under the duplication rule. The cost shrinks from five re-triages to one: only ArgoCD UpdateApplication will re-raise gosecurity:S3649 after the merge, and it is covered by the same checked invariant and by scripts/check-gorm-sql-literal.mjs.

Round 6 frontend: AlertCenter (cc 20 -> 8), ServiceCatalog (17 -> 5) and DeployTaskDetail (25 -> 9) became module-level subcomponents with readonly props shapes and FormInstance-typed form props, following the pattern already used by DeployTaskList and CmdbLabelSchemaList. The extraction is render-identical — the same JSX, the same conditions and the same callbacks — and is pinned by the 230-test unit suite plus the CI-mode build; a local TS-AST cognitive-complexity oracle calibrated against the Sonar HEAD values is used as the resolution bound because the hosted analysis of unchanged lines is only available after the merge.

consumerSpecificControls: SQL literalness in business GORM condition builders is a checked invariant, not a review convention
e2e scripts refuse to run without an explicitly supplied target
deferredCodeIssues: Dependabot-triggered runs still cannot read SONAR_TOKEN, so SonarCloud Scan stays red on Dependabot PRs until Dependabot secrets are provisioned or the job skips that actor; that is a maintainer gate-policy decision.

The Vercel deployment check stays red and is out of scope by maintainer instruction: it is an external GitHub App integration with no committed configuration, its build log needs the Vercel team's credentials, and it is not a required status context on main, so disabling it is a GitHub App or Vercel dashboard action.
sonar.sources=. makes the scanner read PNG evidence files as source text; scoping that property is a Sonar configuration decision left with the maintainer.
No coverage report is produced, which is why sonar.coverage.exclusions=**/* stays in sonar-project.properties on the Free plan.
The ArgoCD UI has no server-registration form, so the new caCert field is reachable only through the API in this round.

The 158-finding CODE_SMELL backlog is addressed in this round rather than deferred; the acceptance oracle is the next hosted analysis, because local linters approximate SonarGo but are not the metric.

biz_argocd_application has no service-instance association, so the reconciler cannot propagate an ArgoCD status into the service-instance state machine without a schema change; the previous TODO stub was deleted instead of faked and the association is a separate design decision.

frontend/scripts/check-menu-contract.mjs resolves seed identifiers only from const blocks, which silently accepts an empty module key for an inline const. The generic checker improvement is base-owned and must be proposed in pantheon-base first (task #38); this round only keeps the ops-side declaration in the shape the current checker understands.
